title: Introduction to Burgundy's Classification System
description: Understand Burgundy's unique four-tier classification, mastering the differences between AOC, Village, Premier Cru and Grand Cru.
lessons.0.title: The AOC Appellation System
lessons.0.content.sections.0.heading: What is AOC?
lessons.0.content.sections.0.text: AOC (Appellation d'Origine Contrôlée) is France's protected origin system, created in 1935 to guarantee that a wine comes from a specific region and follows strict production rules. Since 2009 it has been integrated into the EU's AOP (Appellation d'Origine Protégée), but the AOC label remains in everyday French use.
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.0: Origin demarcation: precise geographical boundaries for vineyards
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.1: Variety restrictions: only permitted grape varieties may be used
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.2: Viticulture rules: maximum yields, planting density, pruning methods
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.3: Winemaking standards: minimum alcohol, ageing requirements
lessons.0.content.sections.0.keyPoints.4: Quality control: chemical analysis plus expert blind tasting
lessons.0.content.sections.1.heading: Burgundy's AOC Architecture
lessons.0.content.sections.1.text: Burgundy has more than 100 AOCs, forming a pyramid from Régionale up to Grand Cru. Each tier has stricter rules on vineyards and yields — the higher the level, the tighter the standards.
lessons.0.content.pyramid.title: Burgundy's Classification Pyramid
lessons.0.content.pyramid.levels.0.name: Grands Crus
lessons.0.content.pyramid.levels.1.name: Premiers Crus
lessons.0.content.pyramid.levels.2.name: Villages
lessons.0.content.pyramid.levels.3.name: Régionales
lessons.0.content.pyramid.levels.3.descr: The Burgundy region as a whole
lessons.0.content.summary: The AOC system guarantees quality and provenance for Burgundy wine, while the classification pyramid clearly reflects the fine-grained differences of terroir.
lessons.1.title: The Four-Tier Classification Explained
lessons.1.content.sections.0.heading: Tier 1: Régionale — Bourgogne
lessons.1.content.sections.0.text: Accounting for 53% of Burgundy's output, this is the entry tier; grapes may come from anywhere within the region. Even though it is the basic level, top producers can craft regional wines of high quality.
lessons.1.content.sections.0.keyPoints.1: Area: roughly 27,000 ha across all of Burgundy
lessons.1.content.sections.0.keyPoints.4: Style: fresh, fruit-driven, easy-drinking everyday wine
lessons.1.content.sections.1.heading: Tier 2: Village
lessons.1.content.sections.1.text: Grapes come from within the boundary of a specific village, expressing that village's character. Burgundy has 44 village-level AOCs, each with its own terroir signature.
lessons.1.content.sections.1.keyPoints.4: Style: village identity with good balance
lessons.1.content.sections.2.heading: Tier 3: Premier Cru
lessons.1.content.sections.2.text: Around 640 plots recognised as superior, usually located on the prime mid-slope. The label must show both the village name and the lieu-dit (vineyard) name.
lessons.1.content.sections.2.keyPoints.0: Label: village name + Premier Cru + vineyard name
lessons.1.content.sections.2.keyPoints.4: Style: high complexity, strong ageing potential, distinct terroir
lessons.1.content.sections.3.heading: Tier 4: Grand Cru
lessons.1.content.sections.3.text: The pinnacle of Burgundy. Only 33 Grand Crus exist (1 in Chablis, 24 in the Côte de Nuits, 8 in the Côte de Beaune). With ideal terroir, these wines can age for decades.
lessons.1.content.sections.3.keyPoints.0: Label: vineyard name only, without village (e.g. Richebourg)
lessons.1.content.sections.3.keyPoints.2: Permitted yields: 35–37 hl/ha for reds (the strictest)
lessons.1.content.sections.3.keyPoints.3: Price range: €100 to tens of thousands of euros per bottle
lessons.1.content.sections.3.keyPoints.4: Style: ultimate complexity, extraordinary ageing potential, unmatched terroir expression
lessons.1.content.sections.3.examples.0: Romanée-Conti (one of the world's most expensive wines)
lessons.1.content.sections.3.examples.3: Clos de Vougeot (the largest Grand Cru, 50 ha)
lessons.1.content.comparisonTable.title: Side-by-Side Comparison of the Four Tiers
lessons.1.content.tips.0: 💡 Quality among Premier Crus in the same village can vary widely — learn each plot's reputation
lessons.1.content.tips.1: 💡 A Grand Cru is not always better than a top producer's Premier Cru — winemaking matters
lessons.1.content.tips.2: 💡 Village wines offer the best value for studying Burgundy terroir
lessons.1.content.tips.3: 💡 Régionales can also surprise, especially from renowned domaines
lessons.1.content.summary: The four-tier system mirrors terroir differences and quality strata, but the producer's craft is equally crucial. Understanding this framework is the first step in appreciating Burgundy wine.
lessons.2.title: How to Read Classification on Wine Labels
lessons.2.content.sections.0.heading: Three Steps to Decode a Label
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.0: Step 1: locate the largest text (usually the classification cue)
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.1: Step 2: check whether a village name is shown
lessons.2.content.sections.0.keyPoints.2: Step 3: confirm if 'Premier Cru' or 'Grand Cru' is stated
lessons.2.content.labelExamples.0.label: GEVREY-CHAMBERTIN
lessons.2.content.labelExamples.1.label: GEVREY-CHAMBERTIN PREMIER CRU 'Clos Saint-Jacques'
lessons.2.content.labelExamples.2.label: CHAMBERTIN GRAND CRU
lessons.2.content.labelExamples.3.label: BOURGOGNE PINOT NOIR
lessons.2.content.labelExamples.4.label: MEURSAULT 1ER CRU
lessons.2.content.practiceQuiz.instructi: Identify the classification of each label below.
lessons.2.content.tips.0: 🔍 Grand Cru labels are the simplest: vineyard name + Grand Cru
lessons.2.content.tips.1: 🔍 A Premier Cru always shows 'Premier Cru' or '1er Cru'
lessons.2.content.tips.2: 🔍 If you see 'Bourgogne', it is regional level
lessons.2.content.tips.3: 🔍 Village wines show only the village name, no vineyard
lessons.2.content.tips.4: 🔍 Font size doesn't equal classification — read the actual words
lessons.2.content.summary: Once you can decode labels, you can quickly judge a wine's tier on the shop shelf and make informed choices.
